name: own.page
tagline: A hosted one-page personal site with links, bio, and embeds, editable without touching code.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: A link-in-bio page is one static HTML document with your face, your name, and a stack of buttons. There is no data to lose, no network to join, and no state to sync: the whole product is layout taste plus hosting you could get free. An agent can produce a config-driven single page site with themes, embeds, and click counting in one sitting, and it will load faster than most hosted equivalents. What you actually buy from the SaaS is not building the page, it is never thinking about it again: a short memorable URL, a phone-friendly editor, and someone else's problem when a link rots. That is a real convenience, just not a technical moat.
coreLoopDIY: Renders a static personal page from a single JSON config with avatar, bio, themed link buttons, social icons, and optional embeds, deployed to free static hosting on a custom domain.
requirements: A domain, or acceptance of a subdomain from your host
A static host such as Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, or GitHub Pages
Optional: a Plausible or Umami instance if you want click analytics
whatYouLose: A visual editor you can use from your phone at 1am
A short, recognizable URL people already trust and click
Professionally tuned templates and typography you did not have to fight with
Built-in analytics, link click tracking, and QR codes without wiring a second service
Someone else handling image hosting, caching, and the day your embed provider changes its API
moatNotes: The polish is real and the hosted URL carries a little social credibility, but neither survives contact with a determined person who owns a domain.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the page is not the point, being findable is. Paying a few dollars a month means the edit takes ninety seconds from a phone, the theme already looks intentional, the analytics tab exists, and nothing breaks silently while you are busy doing the thing the page is supposed to promote. Self-hosting turns a two-minute task into a git commit, which is fine right up until you stop bothering to update it.
notes: Genuinely one of the most one-shottable categories on this site: it is a resume in button form.
prompt:
Build a static personal link-in-bio site. Stack: Astro 4 with TypeScript, zero client framework, plain CSS with custom properties. No React, no Tailwind, no CMS.

Structure:
- src/data/profile.json holds everything editable: name, headline, bio (markdown-lite, allow **bold** and links), avatar path, theme name, ordered links array (label, url, optional icon, optional highlight boolean, optional description), socials array (platform, url), and optional embeds array (type: 'youtube' | 'spotify' | 'form', src).
- src/pages/index.astro reads that JSON at build time and renders the page. No runtime fetching.
- src/styles/themes.css defines four themes via CSS custom properties: 'mono', 'warm', 'midnight', 'brutal'. Theme selected by data-theme attribute on html from profile.json.

Requirements:
- Mobile first, single column, max-width 560px, large tappable link rows with hover and focus states.
- Avatar optimized at build with astro:assets. Fail the build loudly if the avatar file is missing.
- Full SEO and social head tags from profile.json: title, description, canonical, Open Graph, Twitter card. Generate a static og-image.png placeholder note in the README rather than doing dynamic OG rendering.
- Accessibility: real anchor elements, visible focus rings, aria-labels on icon-only social links, passes a keyboard-only walkthrough.
- Inline SVG icon set for common socials in src/components/Icon.astro. No icon font, no external CDN.
- Optional analytics: if PUBLIC_ANALYTICS_SRC and PUBLIC_ANALYTICS_DOMAIN exist in .env, inject that single script tag; otherwise inject nothing. No other telemetry, no cookies, no consent banner needed.
- Add /links.json as a build-time JSON endpoint mirroring the links array, so the data is portable.
- Include a scripts/check-links.mjs that HEAD requests every URL in profile.json and prints dead ones. Wire it as npm run check.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, an admin UI, a database, drag-and-drop editing, click tracking beyond the optional analytics script, multi-page routing, or payments.

Deliver: working npm run dev and npm run build, .env.example, and a README with a 'change your links' section aimed at a future self who has forgotten all of this, plus deploy notes for Cloudflare Pages with a custom domain.
